competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Policy rhetoric firmed into an inflation print that is still ahead. Governor Waller supports a December rate hike and is open to a half-point move if inflation keeps accelerating. Cash SOFR is 3.89 percent. March 2027 SOFR futures imply 4.315, so a higher funds path is already priced rather than a one-day spike. The US ten-year yield is 4.88 and the two-year is 4.56. October consumer prices are due at 8:30 this morning and are not yet known. The dollar is mixed. The kiwi rose 1.26 percent after the incumbent government kept a path to govern, but the kiwi-dollar rate at 0.5613 is still near the bottom of its one-year range. The euro at 1.1193 is historically cheap. The Aussie-kiwi cross fell to 1.228 and remains elevated on a one-year look. Oil marks are WTI 86.85 and Brent 92.57, gold is 4114, and copper is 6.33. The Nasdaq is 25253 and the Dow is 52390, with equity volatility still 25.6 from 6 November. Next is whether the inflation figures validate the hike lean and whether the kiwi bounce extends.

carry-is-king.invalidation: Rebuild the Australia March receive only if, after the inflation figures, the implied rate is back through 4.83 with cash still near 4.85 and the path is no longer threatened by a larger Fed step.
carry-is-king.thesis: The Australia March receive pays only about 3.5 basis points over 4.85 cash, and the mark has already moved against it from 4.83 to 4.88. Waller is leaning into a December hike, oil is firm, and this morning's CPI is still unknown, so that thin cushion does not pay for the gap. The Canada March receive stays: March is 2.885 against cash 2.52, the position is ahead of the 3.00 entry, and cash policy has not changed. AUDNZD is still an elevated cross, and there are no forward points that put spot ahead of cutting the thin Australia receive.

expression_memo.rationale: December SOFR already embeds the public hike, and the unpaid piece is the CPI-conditional larger move. The election move in the kiwi has already printed. Flat is the position.

catalyst-junkie.invalidation: Standing aside fails if December SOFR cheapens to a gap versus cash that no longer covers a 25bp December hike while Waller's hike support is still the public baseline, or if a dated non-CPI event arrives with a known direction.
catalyst-junkie.thesis: SOFR December at 4.165 is about 28 basis points over cash at 3.89, so Waller's already-public support for a December hike is in the front end, and March 2027 at 4.315 adds only another 15 basis points. The half-point line is conditional on inflation still accelerating, and October CPI has not printed, so that residual has no knowable sign. NZDUSD at 0.5613 already rose 1.26 percent on the election result, so the cheap reading is a spent catalyst. The book stays flat.

expression_memo.rationale: AUD weakness is the only aligned close pattern, but the one-day drop is already a large share of the five-day move and there is no close-range level to invalidate against. Flat.

chart-guy.invalidation: The flat call would change if AUDNZD kept falling on both the five-day and one-month closes and a close-based adverse level were available to trade against.
chart-guy.thesis: Five-session and one-month closes disagree on the crosses that actually moved, and the rest are too small to call. USDCAD and NZDCAD have flipped sign between the week and the month, GBPUSD is up on the month and flat on the week, and EURUSD, USDJPY, and NZDUSD are noise on both marks. AUDNZD is the only cross lower on the day, the week, and the month, but the day already did most of that damage and AUDUSD bounced. There is no close-based adverse level to hang a short on, so the book stays flat.

cross-merchant.thesis: AUDNZD at 1.228 is still in the 82nd percentile of its one-year range after a five-day drop of 1.39 percent, so the short from 1.25 is ahead with the richness intact. NZDUSD rose 1.26 percent after the incumbent kept a path to govern and remains near the bottom of its range, while AUDUSD is softer over five days. That governance relief is a New Zealand premium inside a cross that is still historically high. The short cross carries the antipodean split through the US inflation release without taking a direct dollar bet.

dollar-king.thesis: Waller has a December hike in play and is open to 50bp if inflation keeps accelerating, and the strip already leans that way, with cash SOFR at 3.89 versus March 2027 SOFR at 4.315. USDJPY near 158 is around the middle of its one-year range, so that nominal impulse still has room, while the euro, the kiwi, the Swiss franc and the Canadian dollar already embed a rich dollar. October CPI is unknown, and the existing USDJPY long is the dollar expression through the print. WTI at 86.85 leaves USDCAD, already extended, as a finished dollar move.

mean-reverter.thesis: Keep the AUDNZD short. The cross is still high versus its own year, near 1.228 at the 82nd percentile, even after a five-day fall of 1.39 percent, and the fade from 1.25 has only started. The reversal condition is the New Zealand election: the kiwi jumped 1.26 percent and NZDUSD is still around the fourth percentile, so that bid looks like the start of a normalization rather than a completed move. The front end does not offer a better fade. March SOFR at 4.315 versus 3.89 cash is a high funds path, not a cheap receive, and the 32bp 2s10s curve has no catalyst to steepen ahead of an unknown CPI print.

funding_view.current_sofr: Official NY Fed SOFR is 3.89 percent effective 2026-11-06, ACT/360.
funding_view.implication: December SR3 at 4.165 percent is above official SOFR at 3.89 percent, so forward funding is higher, and no expression in front of the unknown morning inflation print beats SOFR charged on shocked risk capital. Flat cash is not alpha.

no-trade-skeptic.invalidation: A delivered CPI outcome that leaves December SR3 or the ten-year mispriced versus a hike path the strip has not already discounted would make risk actionable.
no-trade-skeptic.thesis: Waller's December hike, including openness to 50bp, is already in the strip. March 2027 SOFR implies 4.315 against cash SOFR at 3.89, December SR3 implies 4.165, and the ten-year at 4.88 carries the same message. October CPI is still ahead at 8:30 and unknown, so a rates or dollar position from this clock is a coin flip on shocked capital. NZDUSD sits near the bottom of its range after a bounce, EURUSD is historically cheap, and AUDNZD is still elevated after a five-day fall. Oil at these marks does not clear a funding rate that is set to realize above cash SOFR.

The US 10-year long, in from 5.24 and marked near 4.86, remains the defensive line and stays on, with no add while oil is firm and this morning's CPI is still unknown.
